title: HOPE FOR THE ONE WHO SANK LOW

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'If a foreigner residing among you becomes rich and any of your fellow
Israelites become poor and sell themselves to the foreigner or to a member
of the foreigner's clan, they retain the right of redemption after they have
sold themselves. One of their relatives may redeem them'" - Lev 25:47-48 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is the lowest point imaginable in this chapter. An Israelite becomes so
poor that he sells himself into servitude — and not even to a fellow
Israelite, but to a wealthy foreigner. He has sunk about as low as the social
order allowed. And yet, even here, God says: he retains the right of
redemption. A relative may buy him back.

No situation was beyond the reach of redemption. Even the person who had
fallen to the very bottom, even the one who had sold himself away, could
still be bought back by a willing kinsman.

Dear reader, hold on to this if you feel you have fallen too far. Perhaps you
have made choices that sold you into something you cannot escape. Perhaps you
feel you are the last person redemption could reach. This verse says
otherwise. The right of redemption remained even for the one who had sold
himself away.

That is the gospel. No one is beyond the reach of Christ our Redeemer. Paul
called himself the worst of sinners and then said Christ came to save such as
him (1 Tim 1:15-16). Jesus said He came to seek and to save the lost (Luke
19:10). The thief on the cross, at the very end, was welcomed (Luke 23:43).

However far you have gone, your Redeemer can still reach you. The right of
redemption remains.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I ever feel I have fallen too far for God to reach?
2. What would it mean to believe redemption is still available to me?
3. Who around me feels beyond hope and needs to hear this?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord Jesus, no one is beyond Your reach, not even the one who has fallen
lowest. Thank You that redemption is still available to me. Reach me and hold
me. Amen.
